fields.Name: business-central
fields.Description: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central connector for the REST/OData v4 API v2.0 — finance, sales, purchasing, inventory and master data — with OAuth 2.0 client-credentials (S2S) auth via Microsoft Entra ID and additive runtime $metadata (EDMX) discovery.

Configuration.AuthFlowNote: OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials (S2S / app-only) grant against Microsoft Entra ID. Application permission required: API.ReadWrite.All on the 'Dynamics 365 Business Central' API (distinct from Automation.ReadWrite.All, which only covers the separate, out-of-scope Automation API). Admin-consent step is labeled '(optional)' in Microsoft's own walkthrough -- not confirmed strictly mandatory for a pure app-only grant.
Configuration.AuthHeaderPatternNote: Not shown verbatim in a BC API-call example in the evidence reviewed; standard OAuth2/RFC6750 bearer-token usage implied by the documented client-credentials flow and token endpoint (ImpliedFromExample, not a vendor-literal quote).
Configuration.BasicAuthAccessKeyNote: Web-service access-key (Basic-style) authentication for SOAP/OData web services is documented as deprecated (section header '...(deprecated)' plus repeated INCLUDE deprecation-notice transclusion). Do not build the connector's primary auth path on it.
Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: Client-credentials grants are stateless (no distinct refresh_token) -- a new token is (re)acquired using the client secret whenever the cached one is near/at expiry. PORT RECOMMENDATION (context-empirical, NOT a Microsoft-stated requirement): call acquireTokenByClientCredential per request behind an expiresOn-aware cache (MSAL's ConfidentialClientApplication caches internally, so this is cheap) rather than freezing one token for the life of a long sync. The legacy CDP driver froze the token at connect() with no refresh/expiry check, so long syncs died mid-flight with a 401 surfaced as a generic request error.

PaginationDefaults.mechanism: server-driven paging (continuation tokens) -- vendor explicitly documents this as the mandated mechanism, NOT client-driven $top/$skip
PaginationDefaults.maxPageSizeOnlineNote: Fixed ceiling on Business Central Online; cannot be changed by the tenant.
PaginationDefaults.maxPageSizeOnPrem: configurable via the 'Max Page Size' server setting (CustomSettings.config key ODataServicesMaxPageSize)
PaginationDefaults.continuationLinkJSONKeyNote: UNPROVEN -- no literal occurrence of 'nextLink'/'@odata.nextLink' found anywhere in the acquired ~727-file docs corpus (exhaustive grep, zero hits). Do NOT assume the OASIS-standard '@odata.nextLink' name without a live/sandboxed confirmation -- vendor docs only ever say 'continuation tokens' without naming the JSON property.
PaginationDefaults.topSkipNote: $top/$skip are valid, recognized OData query options in BC's engine, but Microsoft explicitly instructs against using them together for client-driven paging ('there are several problems with this approach and performance is one of them... use server-driven paging'). $top alone (no $skip) is sanctioned for a bounded sample only.

Per-object presence/absence MUST be confirmed by the extractor per IO -- do NOT declare this watermark on every IO from this integration-level candidate alone.

Configuration.BulkOperationsNote: Dedicated JSON-format (NOT multipart/mixed) batch endpoint on the webapi v2.0 surface: POST {prefix}/api/v2.0/$batch, request body {requests:[{method,url,headers,body}]}, response {responses:[{id,status,headers,body}]}. Optional 'Isolation: snapshot' request header makes the whole batch transactional (all-or-nothing revert on any inner-request failure); introduced BC 2020 wave 2 / v17.1. NOT confirmed present on the ODataV4 (Company('{id}')/...) surface -- the only worked $batch example found targets webapi v2.0 specifically, and this matters because Detailed_Customer_Ledger_Entries-style N+1 lookups (observed in the legacy client driver) live on the ODataV4 surface where $batch support is unproven.
Configuration.APIVersioningNote: /api/beta is an unstable surface Microsoft documents may change without notice (out of scope). /api/{publisher}/{group}/{version} is a separate, tenant/extension-specific custom-API path family (see CustomObjectMarkerPattern). v1.0 is superseded by v2.0 (multipart/non-GUID keys replaced by SystemId GUIDs; complex properties flattened); v1.0 OAS YAML retained only as Tier-2 corroboration.

environmentSegmentAmbiguity.status: RESOLVED by RealityProbe re-probe (unauthenticated, read-only, GET only): BOTH forms ROUTE. Form A {server}/v2.0/{tenantId|domain}/{environment}/api/{apiVersion} -> HTTP 401 {"error":{"code":"Unauthorized","message":"The credentials provided are incorrect"}}; Form B {server}/v2.0/{environment}/api/{apiVersion} -> HTTP 401 (same body). Neither returned 404, so both are real, auth-gated prefixes — matching Microsoft documenting both as current and neither as deprecated (api-reference/v2.0/endpoints-apis-for-dynamics.md L28 lists BOTH "/v2.0/<environment name>/api/v2.0" and "/v2.0/<user domain name>/<environment name>/api/v2.0"). The connector MUST parameterise the whole prefix rather than bake either form.
environmentSegmentAmbiguity.adjudicationOwner: ADJUDICATED by RealityProbe (S7) — outcome recorded here, replacing the pending instruction. Every per-object APIPath in this integration ("/companies", "/subscriptions", "/companies({companyId})/timeRegistrationEntries", and the 80 company-scoped siblings) is ROOT-RELATIVE to the Business Central API ROOT — {server}/v2.0/[{tenantId|domain}/]{environment}/api/{apiVersion} — NOT to URLGrammar.webapi.serverBaseConstant on its own. Probe evidence (unauthenticated GET, read-only): the identical paths return HTTP 400 {"error":{"code":"RequestDataInvalid","message":"Request data is invalid."}} when appended directly to https://api.businesscentral.dynamics.com, and HTTP 401 (gated-exists: path real, auth-gated) when appended to EITHER documented API-root form. Docs corroboration: api-reference/v2.0/dynamics-subscriptions.md L29 "POST https://{businesscentralPrefix}/api/v2.0/subscriptions" and api-reference/v2.0/endpoints-apis-for-dynamics.md L28. CONSEQUENCE: the connector base URL (and any future probe --base-url) must be the full API root; the first S7 run used the bare server host, which is what produced the three "wrong" path verdicts — the declared paths themselves are doc-correct and are unchanged by this amendment.
environmentSegmentAmbiguity.openQuestion: STILL OPEN (not resolvable credential-free): whether the dual forms are two interchangeable spellings for the SAME tenant or two DIFFERENT deployment topologies (multi-tenant partner app vs single-tenant direct app). The re-probe cannot separate them — both forms answer 401 before any tenant/environment resolution, so a placeholder tenant GUID yields the same verdict a real one would. Requires a live credential + a real tenant/environment to settle; do NOT pick a canonical form on the 401 evidence alone.

URLGrammar.environmentNameNeverDefaultedNote: {environment} (e.g. 'Production') is tenant-specific runtime connection data, NEVER a baked default. The legacy CDP driver hardcoded 'Production' in getURL(), which meant it could never target a sandbox -- a stage run of the write path posted into the production ledger. This MUST be a required, parameterized per-connection config field with no default value.
URLGrammar.tenantIDSlotNote: UNPROVEN whether {tenantId} must be the Entra AAD tenant GUID specifically, or can also be a domain name -- one doc's 'Direct tenant' connection-method table suggests a domain name is also accepted, but this was not independently re-verified against a live endpoint.

CompanyScoping.scopingBackbone: 81 of 83 enumerated v2.0 entity types nest under companies({companyId}) (or Company('{companyId}') on ODataV4). The 2 exceptions: 'companies' itself (the enumerable company-list root) and 'subscriptions' (global webhook registrations, not company data).
CompanyScoping.companiesEndpointNote: GET companies (or GET /companies) returns the list of companies/tenants reachable by the credential -- a connection can target one configured company via the path segment / query param, or enumerate this list first to discover which companies are reachable.
CompanyScoping.companyAltQueryParam: ?company=<guid> -- alternative to the companies({id}) path segment on the webapi v2.0 surface. NOT confirmed whether the ODataV4 surface also honors this query-param form.
CompanyScoping.discoveryIsAuthoritativeNote: No BC v2.0-specific vendor statement was found asserting that $metadata (either /api/v2.0/$metadata or /ODataV4/$metadata) is a complete, permission-filtered enumeration of every entity/page a given credential can access. Both $metadata endpoints are credential-gated (confirmed HTTP 401 on unauthenticated curl probes) so this build could not inspect their response shape. The one related statement found (for the LEGACY OData/SOAP web-services publishing model, not confirmed to identically apply to the modern v2.0 REST stack) is: 'All authorized users have access to metadata for Business Central web services, but only users who have sufficient Business Central permissions can access actual data' -- i.e. metadata visibility and data access are independent axes, the OPPOSITE direction of 'absence from $metadata proves deactivation'. Per the safe default, absence from $metadata must NEVER be used to deactivate a standard-catalog object.

odataV4TenantPublishedPages.scope: Tenant-published web-service PAGES (e.g. Detailed_Customer_Ledger_Entries) appear here ONLY if that tenant's admin explicitly published them via the Web Services setup page in the BC client -- a per-tenant admin action, NOT a standing vendor-wide contract.
odataV4TenantPublishedPages.note: This surface could not be enumerated at all credential-free. Detailed_Customer_Ledger_Entries was observed live only via one client's bespoke driver (ContextBC.md, context-empirical) -- not confirmed present-by-default on any other tenant. Model as a per-tenant runtime-discovery + Configuration concern, not as static Declared metadata.

ODataQueryCapabilities.n1EliminationNote: $batch (webapi v2.0, JSON form) is the primary documented lever to collapse N+1 per-record lookups, but it is proven ONLY on the webapi v2.0 surface -- NOT proven on the ODataV4 surface where tenant-published pages like Detailed_Customer_Ledger_Entries (the actual N+1 offender observed in the legacy driver) live. Widening a single request's $filter and using multi-level $expand are proven-available complementary levers on webapi v2.0.

httpStatusCodes.429: Too Many Requests -- API request limits exceeded. No documented Retry-After header found in either rate-limit doc reviewed (grep for 'Retry-After' returned zero hits); read it from live response headers, don't assume it's present.
httpStatusCodes.503: OData per-user request-queue timeout -- a request queued behind the max-concurrent-requests-per-user ceiling (5) that waits longer than 8 minutes in the queue (queue capacity 95) is rejected with 503.
httpStatusCodes.504: Gateway Timeout -- request execution exceeded the 10-minute execution limit. Mitigate by splitting requests and handling the resulting 429s with backoff.

ErrorResponseShape.bodyShapeNote: No JSON error-body shape (e.g. an @odata.error-style {code,message} convention) was confirmed anywhere in the evidence reviewed. Do not assume a specific error-body schema without further evidence.
ErrorResponseShape.clientRetryGuidance: Vendor recommends client-side backoff (regular interval, incremental, exponential, or randomized) on 429; no specific algorithm is mandated.

RateLimitPolicy.chosenForBatchFieldsNote: Per-user 'speed rate' (Production: 600 requests/min; Sandbox: 300 requests/min) was chosen as BatchMaxRequestCount/BatchRequestWaitTime because a single OAuth2 client-credentials app registration acts as one 'user'/service principal -- the closest per-app analog BC documents. The alternate, coarser per-environment ceiling (6000 requests per 5-minute sliding window) and the per-user concurrency/connection ceilings below are recorded here for completeness.
RateLimitPolicy.writePacingMsProvenance: context-empirical, NOT a Microsoft-documented limit -- this is the legacy CDP driver's own hardcoded `await this.sleep(500)` before every POST, its ONLY rate control (no 429 retry/handling exists anywhere in that driver). Do not treat 500ms as a vendor-sanctioned pacing value; it is a port artifact worth reviewing, not a floor to preserve blindly.

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: PATCH and DELETE operations require an 'If-Match' header -- either a retrieved ETag value or the wildcard '*' (bypasses the check). Confirmed identical wording recurs across ~20+ *_update.md/*_delete.md per-operation reference pages (e.g. purchaseOrder, itemVariant, project, salesQuote, salesInvoice). When the supplied ETag does not match the current tag, the record is NOT updated/deleted. The literal response-property name for the ETag (commonly '@odata.etag' in OData v4) was NOT independently confirmed in a GET response example within the evidence reviewed -- do not assert that literal property name without further proof. The exact HTTP status code returned on a missing/stale If-Match (commonly 412 Precondition Failed per OData v4 convention) is also not stated by name/number anywhere in the BC docs examined.

WriteCapability.update: Yes -- PATCH, requires an 'If-Match' header (retrieved ETag or '*')
WriteCapability.delete: Yes -- DELETE, requires an 'If-Match' header (retrieved ETag or '*')
WriteCapability.createNote: UNPROVEN in the evidence reviewed -- no fact family confirms POST/Create semantics explicitly (only PATCH/Update and DELETE were evidenced via the recurring If-Match requirement pattern). Do not assume Create support without further evidence.
WriteCapability.batchWrite: Batch write ops are possible through the webapi v2.0 $batch endpoint (each inner request carries its own method/headers/body) -- see BulkOperationsAvailable.

Configuration.DeleteSemanticsNote: UNPROVEN -- no fact family reviewed states whether DELETE performs a hard delete or a soft/archive-flag delete for any BC entity. Left unset; do not assume hard-delete (or soft-delete) without vendor confirmation. This gap also means orphan-deletion sync cannot yet be judged safe.

CustomObjectMarkerPattern.pattern: path-based, NOT name-based: AL-extension-authored custom entities are served under /api/{publisher}/{group}/{version}/... rather than the standard /api/v2.0/... route
CustomObjectMarkerPattern.scope: tenant/extension-specific -- a runtime-discovery concern, not a static vendor-wide catalog fact
CustomObjectMarkerPattern.evidenceNote: Derived from the scoping analysis (SOURCE_STUDY.md), cross-checking the standard v2.0 catalog boundary against this documented custom-API path family; not a direct vendor-doc quote independently re-read verbatim in this pass.

Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerPatternNote: UNPROVEN -- no fact family reviewed describes a marker/prefix convention distinguishing AL-extension-added custom fields from standard fields on an entity (contrast HubSpot's hubspotDefined flag). Left unset.

universalPK.note: Business Central API v2.0 exposes a SystemId GUID as 'id' on nearly every resource (transition-to-api-v2.0.md documents the v1.0->v2.0 migration to GUID SystemId keys). Every per-IOF IsPrimaryKey carries its own addressing-path CODE_EVIDENCE entry; the exceptions are the report-style resources addressed by their subject entity's key (see census).

Configuration.universalPKNote: UNPROVEN -- no fact family reviewed states the literal PK field name BC v2.0 entities expose in their JSON payload (e.g. whether it is 'id', matching the OData v4 / post-v1.0-transition SystemId-GUID-key convention mentioned only in passing for the v1.0-to-v2.0 migration). Left unset rather than assumed; the extractor should confirm this per-object from a resource's own Properties table or a live response.
Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Read-only by default for every object, per standing safety policy -- bidirectional is opt-in and must be validated against a sandbox first (see DefaultConflictResolutionReason for BC-specific preconditions).
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionReason: Conditional recommendation, applicable ONLY if/when bidirectional sync is explicitly opted in for a given object (never the default -- see DefaultSyncDirection). Business Central's documented ETag/If-Match concurrency control (ConcurrencyControl=etag) makes MostRecent a defensible conflict policy for UPDATE conflicts, since the API itself refuses a stale write. However, three preconditions are NOT yet met for turning bidirectional on: (1) DeleteSemantics is UNPROVEN (hard vs soft/archive-flag delete unknown), so orphan-deletion reconciliation cannot be judged safe; (2) the literal ETag response-property name and the exact stale-If-Match status code are both unconfirmed, so client-side stale-write detection logic is unverified against a live response; (3) POST/Create capability is unproven, so a full bidirectional CRUD contract cannot yet be asserted for any object. Do not enable bidirectional for this vendor until all three are resolved (ideally via a live/sandboxed credential).
